━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Feature: Socket-Liveness Watchdog and Service Versioning
  As an operator
  I want the jarvis-serve-nats systemd unit versioned and monitored for socket staleness
  So that I am alerted when the Slack door goes quiet and can trigger self-recovery

  Background:
    Given I have operator access to the jarvis system
    And the jarvis-serve-nats service is running as a systemd user unit
    And the O-30 register exists and is editable

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (4 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core deployment path — establishes the correct unit file in ops
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The versioned systemd unit file is deployed to ops
    Given the current jarvis-serve-nats service configuration is captured
    When I run the coordinator install step
    Then the unit file should be written to ops/systemd/jarvis-serve-nats.service
    And the file should match the running service definition

  # Why: Core monitoring path — watchdog detects quiet door
  @key-example
  Scenario: The watchdog detects a quiet Slack door
    Given the watchdog has been running for the monitoring window
    And no NATS subscription activity has been logged recently
    When the watchdog evaluates journalctl output
    Then the watchdog should report the door as quiet

  # Why: Core alerting path — operator is notified
  @key-example
  Scenario: An alert is posted to Slack when staleness is detected
    Given the watchdog has reported the door as quiet
    When the alerting routine executes
    Then a notification should be posted to the operator Slack channel
    And the notification should describe the detected staleness

  # Why: Core register correction — accurate service naming
  @key-example
  Scenario: The O-30 register is updated with the correct service name
    Given the O-30 register currently lists langgraph dev as the Slack door
    When the register correction routine executes
    Then the register should name serve-nats as the Slack door
    And all other register fields should remain unchanged

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (3 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Just-inside staleness window — should not trigger alert
  @boundary
  Scenario: Recent subscription activity prevents a quiet-door report
    Given the last NATS subscription log entry was 4 minutes ago
    When the watchdog evaluates journalctl output
    Then the watchdog should report the door as active

  # Why: Exactly at staleness threshold — should trigger alert
  @boundary
  Scenario: Subscription inactivity at the exact threshold triggers an alert
    Given the last NATS subscription log entry was exactly 5 minutes ago
    When the watchdog evaluates journalctl output
    Then the watchdog should report the door as quiet

  # Why: Just-outside staleness threshold — confirms boundary enforcement
  @boundary @negative
  Scenario: Subscription inactivity exceeding the threshold triggers an alert
    Given the last NATS subscription log entry was 5 minutes and 1 second ago
    When the watchdog evaluates journalctl output
    Then the watchdog should report the door as quiet

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (3 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Service not running — watchdog should handle gracefully
  @negative
  Scenario: Watchdog handles a stopped service without crashing
    Given the jarvis-serve-nats systemd user unit is inactive
    When the watchdog attempts to read journalctl output
    Then the watchdog should log a service-unavailable condition
    And the watchdog should not post a false quiet-door alert

  # Why: Slack endpoint unreachable — alert failure should be handled
  @negative
  Scenario: Watchdog handles Slack endpoint failure without data loss
    Given the watchdog has detected a quiet door
    When the alerting routine attempts to post to Slack
    Then the watchdog should log the delivery failure
    And the watchdog should queue the alert for retry

  # Why: Register locked — correction should be deferred safely
  @negative
  Scenario: Register correction handles a locked register file
    Given the O-30 register is locked for editing
    When the register correction routine executes
    Then the routine should log a permission-denied condition
    And the register should remain unchanged

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (3 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Concurrent watchdog runs — prevents duplicate alerts
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Concurrent watchdog executions are serialised
    Given two watchdog instances are scheduled to run simultaneously
    When both instances attempt to evaluate journalctl output
    Then only one instance should post an alert
    And the other should skip alerting to avoid duplication

  # Why: Log rotation during monitoring — ensures continuity
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Watchdog handles log rotation without losing detection context
    Given journalctl rotates the service log during monitoring
    When the watchdog reads the next log segment
    Then the watchdog should maintain continuity of the staleness window
    And no false quiet-door report should be generated

  # Why: Rapid service restart — prevents alert flapping
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Watchdog suppresses alerts during rapid restart cycles
    Given the jarvis-serve-nats service restarts multiple times in quick succession
    When the watchdog detects intermittent log gaps
    Then the watchdog should suppress quiet-door alerts until stability is confirmed
